links.outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of chatbot responses to peritoneal dialysis patient questions
links.effect: FRES was 32.6 ± 10.5 for Gemini Pro 2.5, 24.2 ± 11.7 for ChatGPT-5, and 16.2 ± 7.5 for LLaMA Maverick 4 (p < 0.001), all in the difficult-to-read range.
links.quote: Gemini Pro 2.5 achieved higher Flesch Reading Ease (FRES) scores (32.6 ± 10.5) compared with ChatGPT-5 (24.2 ± 11.7) and LLaMA Maverick 4 (16.2 ± 7.5; p < 0.001), as well as higher EQIP scores (75.4% vs. 59.4% and 61.5%, respectively; p < 0.001) and Modified DISCERN scores (4.0 [4.0-4.5] vs. 3.0 [3.0-3.5] and 3.0 [2.5-3.5]; p < 0.001).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the quality, readability, and reliability of LLM-generated responses to peritoneal dialysis questions without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
